title: `voids/stereopsis-void` says Susan Barry "could not picture what she lacked", but Sacks records that as a professor she told him she thought she could, and later wrote "I told you that I thought I could. . . . But I was wrong"; and it says the Mary comparison "belongs to Maria Popova (2024)" though Barry made the grey-to-colour analogy in her first letter, Sacks rejected it in the same essay ("With color, there is no precursor"), and it was linked to Jackson's Mary in print in 2006
